content: Do not fear growing slowly; fear only standing still.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Bu pa man, zhi pa zhan (不怕慢，只怕站) — Classical Folk Adage
explanation: Speed is an idol of the modern world. But in the rhythms of nature, the bamboo spends four years underground barely showing an inch, only to shoot sixty feet in ninety days once its roots are anchored. Slow progress is still progress; absolute standstill is the only true failure.
practicalInsight: If you only wrote one paragraph, walked one mile, or read five pages today, celebrate it. You did not stand still.
reflectionPrompt: Are you judging yourself harshly because your growth is quiet, forgetting that steady drops hollow out stone?
